references.text: The background story of how Moses came to Jethro (Reuel), the priest of Midian, and married his daughter Zipporah.
Jethro is again referred to as Moses' father-in-law, and Moses asks for permission to return to Egypt.
Jethro, the priest of Midian and Moses' father-in-law, comes to Moses in the wilderness after Israel has left Egypt.
Shepherds were an important occupational group among the patriarchs, and Moses continues this tradition.
Horeb is mentioned as God's mountain, where the Lord stood on the rock.
Israel arrives at the Wilderness of Sinai and camps before the mountain, which is identical to Horeb, God's mountain.
Horeb is mentioned as the place where the Lord spoke to the Israelites.
Horeb is referred to as the place where God revealed himself and gave the Ten Commandments.
Elijah traveled to Horeb, God's mountain, where he also met the Lord.
Stephen refers to this event in his speech and mentions Moses as a shepherd and the burning bush at Mount Sinai.
Moses' faith and his time in Midian before leading Israel out of Egypt.
Both verses link Jethro to 'God's mountain' (Horeb/Sinai), but at contrasting times: Moses arrives before the revelation, while Jethro comes after the exodus to meet him there.
Highlights Jethro's role as 'the priest of Midian' (mentioned in 3:1) by showing him performing priestly acts in God's presence together with Israel's leaders.
It is the direct precursor to Exodus 3:1; describes how Moses came to live with Jethro and shepherd his flock before the call at Horeb.
